content.content: Safe sailing depends on clear roles, respectful communication, and tidy habits aboard. Each crewmember contributes by staying aware, using consistent language, and practicing seamanship etiquette.

content: Skipper vs. Crew: Skipper gives commands; crew executes and reports back.
Language: Use short, standard phrases — avoid slang or extra chatter during maneuvers.
Repeat-back: Confirm orders exactly as spoken to ensure accuracy.
Deck Etiquette: Keep lines coiled, gear stowed, and decks clear to prevent accidents.
Questions: If unsure, ask immediately — silence is riskier than speaking up.
Respect: Acknowledge each person’s task and avoid cross-talk when commands are active.

sideB.content: Skipper gives commands, crew executes with repeat-back; use short, clear phrases; keep decks tidy; ask if unsure; respect roles and avoid cross-talk.

content.content: Use simple, unambiguous commands acknowledged back word‑for‑word to reduce errors.
